title: The Fox and the Monkey
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Fox and a Monkey were on the road together, and fell into a dispute as to which of the two was the better born. They kept it up for some time, till they came to a place where the road passed through a cemetery full of monuments, when the Monkey stopped and looked about him and gave a great sigh. "Why do you sigh?" said the Fox. The Monkey pointed to the tombs and replied, "All the monuments that you see here were put up in honour of my forefathers, who in their day were eminent men." The Fox was speechless for a moment, but quickly recovering he said, "Oh! don't stop at any lie, sir; you're quite safe: I'm sure none of your ancestors will rise up and expose you."
Boasters brag most when they cannot be detected.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Fox and Monkey argue about on the road?
options: Which of the two could run faster
Which of the two deserved more food
Which of the two was the better born
Which of the two knew the road better

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the road pass that makes the Monkey stop?
options: Through a cemetery full of monuments
Across a narrow wooden bridge
Beside a grand old palace
Through a busy marketplace

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Monkey do when he sees the monuments?
options: He laughs loudly at their appearance
He runs ahead without stopping
He asks the Fox to read the inscriptions aloud
He stops, looks about, and gives a great sigh

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Monkey claim about the monuments?
options: That they mark the graves of famous foxes
That they were put up in honour of his forefathers
That his family built them long ago
That they were stolen from a rival family

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Monkey describe his forefathers?
options: As humble farmers and traders
As wandering monkeys with no fixed home
As eminent men in their day
As soldiers who died in battle

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox say the Monkey is quite safe from?
options: His ancestors rising up to expose his lie
Being caught lying by other travellers
Being punished for entering the cemetery
Losing the argument about noble birth

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Fox call the Monkey's claim a lie without directly proving it false?
options: He has personally researched the Monkey's family history
He has visited this cemetery many times before
He recognizes the names carved on the monuments
He recognizes that no dead ancestor can contradict a false claim about them

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Monkey choose this particular moment to make his claim?
options: He genuinely recognizes his family's names on the tombs
The cemetery gives him a convenient, unverifiable backdrop for his boast
He wants to end the argument by changing the subject entirely
He is asked directly by the Fox to prove his noble birth

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "eminent" mean in "who in their day were eminent men"?
options: Wealthy beyond measure
Feared by their enemies
Distinguished or well-known
Related to royalty

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: People often exaggerate most freely when no one can check what they claim
Monuments are the most reliable proof of a family's noble birth
Foxes are always more honest than monkeys in an argument
Arguments about ancestry are rarely worth having at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how long do the Fox and Monkey keep up their dispute?
options: Only a few moments
For the entire journey without pause
Until they reached their destination
For some time

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what question does the Fox ask when the Monkey sighs?
options: "What troubles you?"
"Why do you sigh?"
"Are you unwell?"
"What do you see there?"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Fox react just before making his reply?
options: He laughs out loud immediately
He walks away without answering
He is speechless for a moment
He asks the Monkey to repeat himself

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the Fox's brief silence before responding be significant?
options: It shows he is caught off guard by such a bold, unprovable claim
It shows he genuinely believes the Monkey's story
It shows he is trying to remember his own family history
It shows he is afraid to challenge the Monkey directly

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Fox's remark about the Monkey's ancestors imply about the reliability of the Monkey's story?
options: It has already been proven true by the monuments themselves
It has been confirmed by other animals along the road
It was written down somewhere the Fox has read before
It cannot be checked, since the dead cannot speak up to deny it

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "expose" mean in "none of your ancestors will rise up and expose you"?
options: Physically harm someone
Reveal the truth about someone
Praise someone publicly
Introduce someone to a stranger

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Fox and a Monkey discover their true family history together
A Monkey proves his noble birth using the cemetery's monuments
A Monkey boasts of noble ancestors buried nearby, and the Fox mocks the unprovable claim
A Fox apologizes for doubting the Monkey's ancestry
